Coordinate choice and object scale change the apparent direction and wavelength; diffuse variation should remain attached to the surface when the light moves, while specular highlights can move.
16	**Executable Method:** `appearance.directional_stone(name, scale, colors, roughness, distortion)` creates an editable procedural Blender material using object coordinates, axis scaling, a noise texture and a color ramp; returns the material. Adjust scale/axes for streak direction; apply or account for object transforms. For another candidate use an independently authored UV/image mapping with appropriate color space and packing, and a roughness-only candidate. # Editable reconstruction capability library

Use the reference as a set of image constraints, not a unique 3D truth. Establish a scale convention; hidden geometry, absolute scale, and lighting/material decomposition are ambiguous. Iterate with a fixed camera before jointly adjusting camera and layout. Keep candidate source, renders, settings, and decisions; never silently overwrite the baseline. See capabilities.json for callable modules. These methods are hypotheses and have not been independently validated on unseen scenes.

## Capability Name: Camera-layout and articulated occlusion reasoning
**Applicable Conditions:** A large object, doorway, furniture, or wall has the wrong silhouette, depth order, or visibility.
**Problem and Technical Hypotheses:** An edge-on face, intervening wall, incorrect hinge, or camera projection can each hide the same object. Image evidence includes visible contour, floor occlusion, wall junctions, semantic orientation, and neighboring landmarks; it does not identify the hidden room. 
**Executable Method:** `spatial.project_points(scene, camera, points)` returns normalized camera projections and camera-space depth, using Blender's world-to-camera projection. `spatial.hinge_positions(hinge, width, angles, local_direction)` provides candidate free-edge locations in world XY. Specify radians and world units. Build a leaf and its details as children of a pivot at the jamb; the opening must be an actual opening, not a dark patch over solid wall. Compare swings at fixed camera first; then if necessary vary camera pose and focal length together with room dimensions. Rank reference landmarks, visible face width, relative scale, edges and occlusion, not one contour alone. Keep furniture positions coherent and parent leaf details to the hinge.
**Verification Method:** Render camera comparisons with identical lighting; temporarily hide only the suspected wall, then restore it. Inspect top and side views of *the selected* assembly, including the full swing arc, hinge to jamb alignment, opening, walls, furniture, and floor. Check projected points for positive camera depth and inspect clipping. Validate after any camera or layout revision.
**Failure Conditions and Side Effects:** Projection ignores occlusion and lens distortion; hinge helper assumes a vertical axis. Better visible leaf width alone does not justify a displaced hinge or a leaf wider than its opening. Isolated or obstructed views cannot prove absence of intersections. Single-view matching can compromise other landmarks.
**Evidence and Knowledge Origin:** General projective geometry and articulation prior; historical door trials in both repetitions motivate visibility isolation and candidate comparison. One selected case had an obstructed side diagnostic, so coherence was not established; do not treat that placement as a repair recipe. Details in research evidence.

## Capability Name: Material mapping versus illumination experiment
**Applicable Conditions:** A surface appears too uniform, too streaky, or wrongly oriented.
**Problem and Technical Hypotheses:** Surface color, roughness, illumination, and geometry can produce similar marks. Coordinate choice and object scale change the apparent direction and wavelength; diffuse variation should remain attached to the surface when the light moves, while specular highlights can move.
**Executable Method:** `appearance.directional_stone(name, scale, colors, roughness, distortion)` creates an editable procedural Blender material using object coordinates, axis scaling, a noise texture and a color ramp; returns the material. Scale is a three-vector in local coordinate units, and colors are linear RGBA. Assign explicitly to the intended material slot. Adjust scale/axes for streak direction; apply or account for object transforms. For another candidate use an independently authored UV/image mapping with appropriate color space and packing, and a roughness-only candidate. Compare all under identical camera, exposure, geometry and render settings, then move a light independently. Do not assume object coordinates are meters after object scaling; seams and texture direction on edges need inspection.
**Verification Method:** Compare reference-aligned crops and full-frame renders for spatial frequency, contrast, coverage, edge continuity, orientation and neighboring brightness; compare each candidate under both light directions. Use neutral light and color management consistently. Record what moved and what did not; change one factor at a time.
**Failure Conditions and Side Effects:** A procedural node network or image texture is not evidence of improvement. Highlights and indirect light also depend on roughness, geometry and camera; light tests do not uniquely decompose appearance. Object-space mapping may distort on nonuniform scale; image coordinates may stretch or clamp on edges.
**Evidence and Knowledge Origin:** Both historical material runs rendered color, image and roughness candidates under alternate lighting and retained image candidates. Procedural implementation here is an independently written general hypothesis, not their selected texture or a proven transfer.

## Capability Name: Support and assembly diagnostics
**Applicable Conditions:** An object may float, penetrate a support, or disconnect after a repair.
**Problem and Technical Hypotheses:** Bounding boxes conflate support with proximity and do not show true contact. An assembly can be connected internally yet float, or rest on a floor while components are disconnected.
**Executable Method:** `support.sample_support(obj, supports, tolerance, band, ray_margin)` samples evaluated mesh vertices in a low-Z band, casting vertically from above each sample onto the supplied evaluated mesh supports. Returns per-sample signed vertical gaps and a conservative category. World Z is up; supports must be explicitly supplied. A negative gap is only *possible* penetration. Missing rays yield unknown; near-zero is not proof of physical contact. `support.world_bounds(obj)` provides evaluated bounds for broad-phase checking only. Move a complete assembly or redesign its feet as separate candidates rather than blindly snapping individual parts.
**Verification Method:** Inspect all feet/wheels, full sample coverage, local supports, side views, clearance, and changed silhouette; repeat after the selected repair. Separately inspect joints (wheel/fork, fork/spoke, post/seat), including top/side views and evaluated geometry. Use denser surface sampling or mesh intersection testing for critical results; rays and vertices alone can miss intersections, overhangs, or unsupported areas.
**Failure Conditions and Side Effects:** Downward ray tests assume an appropriate horizontal support and do not establish stability, exact contact, connectivity, or volume intersection. The highest hit can be a top surface above the object; ray margin must exceed geometry thickness. Modifiers and sparse meshes affect sampling. Unknown is not a pass.
**Evidence and Knowledge Origin:** Historical chair runs compared whole-chair lowering against caster changes with evaluated wheel samples and side views. Their numerical checks are sampled estimates, not a physics proof; prior knowledge supplies the interpretation boundaries.

"""Parameterized camera projection and vertical-hinge candidate helpers for Blender."""
import math
from mathutils import Vector
from bpy_extras.object_utils import world_to_camera_view


def project_points(scene, camera, points):
    """Return dictionaries of normalized image coordinates and signed camera depth."""
    inv = camera.matrix_world.inverted()
    out = []
    for p in points:
        p = Vector(p)
        uv = world_to_camera_view(scene, camera, p)
        out.append({'x': uv.x, 'y': uv.y, 'depth': -(inv @ p).z,
                    'inside_frame': 0 <= uv.x <= 1 and 0 <= uv.y <= 1 and uv.z > 0})
    return out


def hinge_positions(hinge, width, angles, local_direction=(1, 0)):
    """Free edge positions for angles in radians, hinge world XYZ, direction XY."""
    if width <= 0:
        raise ValueError('width must be positive')
    x, y = local_direction
    n = math.hypot(x, y)
    if not n:
        raise ValueError('local direction must be nonzero')
    x, y = x/n, y/n
    return [(hinge[0] + width*(x*math.cos(a)-y*math.sin(a)),
             hinge[1] + width*(x*math.sin(a)+y*math.cos(a)), hinge[2]) for a in angles]

"""Small editable directional material hypothesis; no scene-specific assets."""
import bpy


def directional_stone(name, scale=(3.0, 0.7, 1.0),
                      colors=((0.6, 0.61, 0.6, 1), (0.9, 0.9, 0.89, 1)),
                      roughness=0.45, distortion=0.3):
    if len(scale) != 3 or len(colors) != 2:
        raise ValueError('scale needs three components and colors two RGBA values')
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nodes = mat.node_tree.nodes
    links = mat.node_tree.links
    bsdf = nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = roughness
    coord = nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
    multiply = nodes.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath')
    multiply.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
    multiply.inputs[1].default_value = scale
    noise = nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
    noise.inputs['Distortion'].default_value = distortion
    ramp = nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
    ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color = colors[0]
    ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color = colors[1]
    links.new(coord.outputs['Object'], multiply.inputs[0])
    links.new(multiply.outputs['Vector'], noise.inputs['Vector'])
    links.new(noise.outputs['Fac'], ramp.inputs['Fac'])
    links.new(ramp.outputs['Color'], bsdf.inputs['Base Color'])
    return mat

1	"""Sampled world-vertical support diagnostics, not a contact solver."""
2	import bpy
3	from mathutils import Vector
4	from mathutils.bvhtree import BVHTree
5	
6	
7	def _vertices(obj, dg):
8	    ev = obj.evaluated_get(dg)
9	    mesh = ev.to_mesh()
10	    try:
11	        return [ev.matrix_world @ v.co for v in mesh.vertices]
12	    finally:
13	        ev.to_mesh_clear()
14	
15	
16	def world_bounds(obj):
17	    """Return world-space minimum and maximum evaluated vertex coordinates."""
18	    vertices = _vertices(obj, bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get())
19	    if not vertices:
20	        return None
21	    return (tuple(min(v[i] for v in vertices) for i in range(3)),
22	            tuple(max(v[i] for v in vertices) for i in range(3)))
23	
24	
25	def sample_support(obj, supports, tolerance=0.001, band=0.001, ray_margin=10.0):
26	    """Return sampled gaps and classification; unknown for any missing support ray."""
27	    if tolerance < 0 or band < 0 or ray_margin <= 0:
28	        raise ValueError('nonnegative tolerance/band and positive margin required')
29	    dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
30	    vertices = _vertices(obj, dg)
31	    if not vertices or not supports:
32	        return {'category': 'unknown support', 'gaps': [], 'misses': 0}
33	    low = min(v.z for v in vertices)
34	    samples = [v for v in vertices if v.z <= low + band]
35	    trees = []
36	    for support in supports:
37	        ev = support.evaluated_get(dg)
38	        mesh = ev.to_mesh()
39	        try:
40	            vs = [ev.matrix_world @ v.co for v in mesh.vertices]
41	            faces = [tuple(p.vertices) for p in mesh.polygons]
42	            if vs and faces:
43	                trees.append(BVHTree.FromPolygons(vs, faces, all_triangles=False))
44	        finally:
45	            ev.to_mesh_clear()
46	    gaps, misses = [], 0
47	    for v in samples:
48	        origin = Vector((v.x, v.y, v.z + ray_margin))
49	        hits = [tree.ray_cast(origin, Vector((0, 0, -1)), 2*ray_margin)[0] for tree in trees]
50	        hits = [p for p in hits if p is not None]
51	        if hits:
52	            gaps.append(v.z - max(p.z for p in hits))
53	        else:
54	            misses += 1
55	    if misses or not gaps:
56	        category = 'unknown support'
57	    elif min(gaps) < -tolerance:
58	        category = 'possible penetration'
59	    elif min(gaps) > tolerance:
60	        category = 'positive gap'
61	    else:
62	        category = 'near-zero sample'
63	    return {'category': category, 'gaps': gaps, 'misses': misses, 'samples': len(samples)}
64

sys.path.insert(0, '/app/library')
import bpy
from mathutils import Vector
import spatial, support, appearance
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT'); bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=2, location=(0,0,-1)); floor=bpy.context.object
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=2, location=(0,0,2)); obj=bpy.context.object
bpy.context.view_layer.update()
assert support.sample_support(obj,[floor])['category']=='positive gap'
obj.location.z=1; bpy.context.view_layer.update()
assert support.sample_support(obj,[floor])['category']=='near-zero sample'
obj.location.z=.9; bpy.context.view_layer.update()
assert support.sample_support(obj,[floor])['category']=='possible penetration'
obj.location.x=10; bpy.context.view_layer.update()
assert support.sample_support(obj,[floor])['category']=='unknown support'
assert support.world_bounds(obj) is not None
assert abs(spatial.hinge_positions((0,0,0),1,[math.pi/2])[0][1]-1)<1e-6
bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0,0,10)); camera=bpy.context.object
bpy.context.view_layer.update()
assert spatial.project_points(bpy.context.scene,camera,[(0,0,0)])[0]['depth']>0
mat=appearance.directional_stone('synthetic'); assert mat.use_nodes and mat.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
print('LIBRARY_SYNTHETIC_CHECK_PASS')

import sys, math, json
sys.path.insert(0,'/app/library')
import bpy
from mathutils import Vector
import spatial, support, appearance
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT'); bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)
def box(name, loc, scale):
 bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=2, location=loc); o=bpy.context.object; o.name=name; o.scale=scale; return o
floor=box('floor',(0,0,-.1),(4,4,.1)); leg=box('leg',(0,0,1),(.1,.1,1)); bpy.context.view_layer.update()
for z in (1.2,1,.9):
 leg.location.z=z; bpy.context.view_layer.update(); print('SUPPORT',z,support.sample_support(leg,[floor]))
leg.location.x=8; bpy.context.view_layer.update(); print('MISS',support.sample_support(leg,[floor])); print('BOUNDS',support.world_bounds(leg))
print('HINGE',spatial.hinge_positions((1,2,0),2,[0,math.pi/2]));
try: spatial.hinge_positions((0,0,0),0,[0])
except ValueError as e: print('EXPECTED_EXCEPTION',str(e))
bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0,0,10)); cam=bpy.context.object; bpy.context.view_layer.update(); print('PROJECTION',spatial.project_points(bpy.context.scene,cam,[(0,0,0),(0,0,11)]))
mat=appearance.directional_stone('probe'); leg.data.materials.append(mat)
print('MATERIAL_BINDING',leg.material_slots[0].material.name,'LINKS',[(l.from_node.bl_idname,l.from_socket.name,l.to_node.bl_idname,l.to_socket.name) for l in mat.node_tree.links]); print('IMAGE_RESOURCES',[(n.name,n.image.name if n.image else None) for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.bl_idname=='ShaderNodeTexImage'])
# Limited selection-inspired editable table and articulated door; not a reconstruction.
leg.location=(0,0,1); top=box('tabletop',(0,0,2.05),(1.3,.7,.05)); pivot=bpy.data.objects.new('hinge',None); bpy.context.collection.objects.link(pivot); pivot.location=(3,0,0)
leaf=box('door_leaf',(0,0,0),(0.5,.04,1)); leaf.parent=pivot; leaf.location=(.5,0,1); detail=box('door_detail',(0,0,0),(.1,.01,.2)); detail.parent=leaf; detail.location=(0,1.1,0)
for a in (0,math.pi/4):
 pivot.rotation_euler.z=a; bpy.context.view_layer.update(); print('ASSEMBLY',a,'hinge',tuple(pivot.matrix_world.translation),'leaf',tuple(leaf.matrix_world.translation),'detail',tuple(detail.matrix_world.translation),'edge_prediction',spatial.hinge_positions(tuple(pivot.location),1,[a]))
print('TABLE_SUPPORT',support.sample_support(leg,[floor])); print('AABB_ONLY',support.world_bounds(top),support.world_bounds(leaf))
bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath='/app/selection_probe.blend')
print('PROBE_COMPLETE')

# Editable reconstruction capability library

Use the reference as a set of image constraints, not a unique 3D truth. Establish a scale convention; hidden geometry, absolute scale, and lighting/material decomposition are ambiguous. Iterate with a fixed camera before jointly adjusting camera and layout. Keep candidate source, renders, settings, and decisions; never silently overwrite the baseline. See capabilities.json for callable modules. These methods are hypotheses and have not been independently validated on unseen scenes.

## Capability Name: Camera-layout and articulated occlusion reasoning
**Applicable Conditions:** A large object, doorway, furniture, or wall has the wrong silhouette, depth order, or visibility.
**Problem and Technical Hypotheses:** An edge-on face, intervening wall, incorrect hinge, or camera projection can each hide the same object. Image evidence includes visible contour, floor occlusion, wall junctions, semantic orientation, and neighboring landmarks; it does not identify the hidden room. 
**Executable Method:** `spatial.project_points(scene, camera, points)` returns normalized camera projections and camera-space depth, using Blender's world-to-camera projection. `spatial.hinge_positions(hinge, width, angles, local_direction)` provides candidate free-edge locations in world XY. Specify radians and world units. Build a leaf and its details as children of a pivot at the jamb; the opening must be an actual opening, not a dark patch over solid wall. Compare swings at fixed camera first; then if necessary vary camera pose and focal length together with room dimensions. Rank reference landmarks, visible face width, relative scale, edges and occlusion, not one contour alone. Keep furniture positions coherent and parent leaf details to the hinge.
**Verification Method:** Render camera comparisons with identical lighting; temporarily hide only the suspected wall, then restore it. Inspect top and side views of *the selected* assembly, including the full swing arc, hinge to jamb alignment, opening, walls, furniture, and floor. Check projected points for positive camera depth and inspect clipping. Validate after any camera or layout revision.
**Failure Conditions and Side Effects:** Projection ignores occlusion and lens distortion; hinge helper assumes a vertical axis. Better visible leaf width alone does not justify a displaced hinge or a leaf wider than its opening. Isolated or obstructed views cannot prove absence of intersections. Single-view matching can compromise other landmarks.
**Evidence and Knowledge Origin:** General projective geometry and articulation prior; historical door trials in both repetitions motivate visibility isolation and candidate comparison. One selected case had an obstructed side diagnostic, so coherence was not established; do not treat that placement as a repair recipe. Details in research evidence.

## Capability Name: Material mapping versus illumination experiment
**Applicable Conditions:** A surface appears too uniform, too streaky, or wrongly oriented.
**Problem and Technical Hypotheses:** Surface color, roughness, illumination, and geometry can produce similar marks. Coordinate choice and object scale change the apparent direction and wavelength; diffuse variation should remain attached to the surface when the light moves, while specular highlights can move.
**Executable Method:** `appearance.directional_stone(name, scale, colors, roughness, distortion)` creates an editable procedural Blender material using object coordinates, axis scaling, a noise texture and a color ramp; returns the material. Scale is a three-vector in local coordinate units, and colors are linear RGBA. Assign explicitly to the intended material slot. Adjust scale/axes for streak direction; apply or account for object transforms. For another candidate use an independently authored UV/image mapping with appropriate color space and packing, and a roughness-only candidate. Compare all under identical camera, exposure, geometry and render settings, then move a light independently. Do not assume object coordinates are meters after object scaling; seams and texture direction on edges need inspection.
**Verification Method:** Compare reference-aligned crops and full-frame renders for spatial frequency, contrast, coverage, edge continuity, orientation and neighboring brightness; compare each candidate under both light directions. Use neutral light and color management consistently. Record what moved and what did not; change one factor at a time.
**Failure Conditions and Side Effects:** A procedural node network or image texture is not evidence of improvement. Highlights and indirect light also depend on roughness, geometry and camera; light tests do not uniquely decompose appearance. Object-space mapping may distort on nonuniform scale; image coordinates may stretch or clamp on edges.
**Evidence and Knowledge Origin:** Both historical material runs rendered color, image and roughness candidates under alternate lighting and retained image candidates. Procedural implementation here is an independently written general hypothesis, not their selected texture or a proven transfer.

## Capability Name: Support and assembly diagnostics
**Applicable Conditions:** An object may float, penetrate a support, or disconnect after a repair.
**Problem and Technical Hypotheses:** Bounding boxes conflate support with proximity and do not show true contact. An assembly can be connected internally yet float, or rest on a floor while components are disconnected.
**Executable Method:** `support.sample_support(obj, supports, tolerance, band, ray_margin)` samples evaluated mesh vertices in a low-Z band, casting vertically from above each sample onto the supplied evaluated mesh supports. Returns per-sample signed vertical gaps and a conservative category. World Z is up; supports must be explicitly supplied. A negative gap is only *possible* penetration. Missing rays yield unknown; near-zero is not proof of physical contact. `support.world_bounds(obj)` provides evaluated bounds for broad-phase checking only. Move a complete assembly or redesign its feet as separate candidates rather than blindly snapping individual parts.
**Verification Method:** Inspect all feet/wheels, full sample coverage, local supports, side views, clearance, and changed silhouette; repeat after the selected repair. Separately inspect joints (wheel/fork, fork/spoke, post/seat), including top/side views and evaluated geometry. Use denser surface sampling or mesh intersection testing for critical results; rays and vertices alone can miss intersections, overhangs, or unsupported areas.
**Failure Conditions and Side Effects:** Downward ray tests assume an appropriate horizontal support and do not establish stability, exact contact, connectivity, or volume intersection. The highest hit can be a top surface above the object; ray margin must exceed geometry thickness. Modifiers and sparse meshes affect sampling. Unknown is not a pass.
**Evidence and Knowledge Origin:** Historical chair runs compared whole-chair lowering against caster changes with evaluated wheel samples and side views. Their numerical checks are sampled estimates, not a physics proof; prior knowledge supplies the interpretation boundaries.
